newsitem.title: NORWAY: Troll C licensees opt to land oil line at Mongstad.
newsitem.headline: Troll C licensees opt to land oil line at Mongstad.

text.p: The licensees of the North Sea Troll C development have opted to use the Mongstad oil terminal on the west coast of Norway as the landfall for a new crude pipeline from field, Den norske stats oljeselskap ASA said on Thursday.
The 90-kilometre pipeline will cost around 500 million crowns and will have a capacity of around 200,000 barrels per day, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The line will begin operation in October, 1999, when operator Norsk Hydro ASA brings Troll C on stream from the thin oil zone in the Troll West gas province.

"We opted for this solution after comparing tariffs between Mongstad and the nearby Sture facility," said Oeyvind Kirkhus, Troll licence coordinator. "Mongstad came out a little cheaper and could also offer somewhat better flexibility."
Operator of the pipeline has still to be decided, Statoil said. The state oil company already operates the Troll Oil Pipeline from the Troll B development.
